original_question: For feedback-controlled flashing ratchets, can the general thermodynamic results of [13] be applied to determine the maximum entropy reduction these ratchets can achieve and to establish a full thermodynamic description of such systems?
target_in_paper: Section III.2 (Lines 140–142) of the paper states: “The application of the results of [19†cao09] to feedback controlled flashing ratchets has not been done yet. It will allow to establish bounds on the entropy reduction attainable for feedback flashing ratchet and to establish the thermodynamics of these systems, which are theoretically and technologically relevant. Therefore, this is another relevant open problem.”
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the system under study (feedback-controlled flashing ratchets), the intent to apply the general thermodynamic (entropy reduction) results of Cao & Feito (2009), and the objectives of determining the maximum entropy reduction and establishing a full thermodynamic description.
missing_details: Exact statement of the general thermodynamic results (Eqs. (14) and (15)) relating average entropy reduction ΔS_info to mutual informations I(C_k;X_k|C_{1:k-1}) and definitions of macrostates X_k and control actions C_k
Specification of the flashing ratchet model: discrete‐time on/off switching of a periodic potential based on measurements of the sign of the net force on N Brownian particles
Definition of the control protocol parameters: number of control steps M or time duration T, measurement interval τ, and information per step
Clarification of “full thermodynamic description” (e.g., expressions for extractable work, heat flow, and efficiency under isothermal conditions)
Definition of the non-redundant information rate İ=lim_{T→∞}1/T I(C_{1:N};X_{1:N}) and its role in restating performance bounds
Reference to the existing performance bounds J_closed–J_open≤C√I and P_closed–P_open≤D I (Eqs. (5) and (6)) and the open question of restating them in terms of İ
refined_question: In a feedback-controlled flashing ratchet where at each discrete time step τ a controller measures the sign of the net force on N Brownian particles and switches a spatially periodic potential on or off, can the general entropy reduction formalism of Cao & Feito (2009) — which proves that the total average entropy reduction due to M control steps is ΔS_info=∑_{k=1}^M I(C_k;X_k|C_{1:k-1}) (Section II.4) — be applied to derive an explicit upper bound on the average entropy reduction rate ΔS_info/T for this ratchet? Furthermore, can this bound, together with a restatement of the previously obtained performance relations J_closed–J_open≤C √I and P_closed–P_open≤D I (Section II.3) in terms of the non-redundant information rate İ=lim_{T→∞}1/T I(C_{1:N};X_{1:N}), be used to establish a complete thermodynamic description of the feedback-controlled flashing ratchet under isothermal conditions, including limits on extractable work, heat flow, and efficiency?
justification: The refined question directly quotes and cites the open problem in Section III.2, explicitly defines the ratchet model, specifies the thermodynamic results (Eqs. (14) and (15)), incorporates the performance bounds (Eqs. (5) and (6)), and introduces the non-redundant information rate, making the question fully self-contained and faithful to the paper’s intent.
